Great for Natural Cycles, But Missing Support for IVF & IUI. Fertility and infertility are complex journeys. I imagine many women using Premom are, like me, navigating the challenges of conceiving and turning to this app because it’s comprehensive and helps us understand our natural cycles.

That said, it would be incredible if Premom expanded its features to better support those going through IVF or IUI. Having the ability to integrate lab results alongside home tests, with charts that paint the bigger picture, would make this app truly invaluable. Right now, it feels like Premom is so close to “having it all,” but it falls short for those of us with diagnosed infertility.

Inclusivity in this space matters broadening support for IVF and IUI would expand your reach and make the app a trusted companion for a wider community. It would also mean a lot if these features weren’t hidden behind additional fees, as fertility treatments are already financially and emotionally overwhelming.

Premom is on the right track please take the next step to make it a resource for all women on their fertility journey.

Great, but not perfect…. I absolutely love this app. I have PCOS and had been TTC for years unsuccessfully. In 2022 I had an early miscarriage and the doctor that I saw told me about the app as she had similar issues. I began using the app to track bbt and LH and got pregnant with my rainbow baby. 

The community on the app is great and there are a ton of great features, but the one thing that prevents me from giving the app 5 stars is that it doesn’t take into account people with abnormal cycles when predicting the ovulation window and next period. 

I understand initially not being able to predict for someone with an abnormal cycle length, but if the person is continuously using the app and tracking LH and their periods, it should after a couple cycles. If you see a pattern in the cycle length the app should be able to start predicting based on the records. For example with help from medication, my cycles are starting to be a little bit more normal as far as predictability goes even though my average cycle is 71 to 72 days which is still abnormal. 

Even though I continuously track, and you can clearly see that my cycle days are up to that point consistently the app still predicts my fertile window to be about five days after the last date of my menstrual cycle and then it tells me I’m in the two week wait. During this time it tells me to keep checking and testing to see if I’m pregnant, which can get annoying, especially because it pops up when you get close to the end of the two week wait it asks when you open up the app in the morning if you took a pregnancy test and if I say no, it’s telling me I should test which I know I shouldn’t because I know I have an ovulated yet. 

I understand the app, not being able to predict if somebody really truly does have irregular cycles where one cycle is 60 days and then the next one is 180 days. In that situation it makes sense that the app wouldn’t be able to predict because there’s no consistency, but the fact that when there is consistency it’s just not fitting into the normal range, the app still can’t manage to do a more accurate prediction is frustrating.

Even with this issue, I still find this app to be better than others. I have tried and as I mentioned, I was able to successfully get pregnant and have my rainbow baby by using this application. I will continue to use this app going forward because it does help and most things about it are fantastic. I hope that this helps anyone who has abnormal cycle length or irregular cycles as well. I also hope that’s the makers and designers a Premom will see this and help fix this issue since there seems to be a large number of individuals with PCOS that use the application.
